criteria.evidence: All required sections are present and substantive: What it does ("When it runs: a play is about to plan, break down or build from the ICE of a node"), Inputs / Outputs (spine fields, intent pages' "**Stage:**" line, --done, --node, JSON out, exit codes 0/1/2), Rules & behavior (11 branches), Acceptance criteria (8 Given/When/Then), Out of scope (4 items with owners), and a full Agent intent (ICE) with every label.

"A met intent counts, because it was confirmed first. Work that keeps it met is still wanted."; "A missing business intent page counts as not confirmed. Thus a link to an intent that nobody wrote never makes a node ready."; "The check reads only files. It uses no git, no network and no model call. Thus the same model always gives the same answer."; "The warning asks for the link. The not-ready answer stops work until the link exists."

Rules are discrete bullets, one branch each; acceptance is strict Given/When/Then, e.g. "Given an id that is not in the spine, when the check runs with `--node`, then it exits 2."; the function is stated as behavior ("For each capability and functionality, it answers 'ready' or 'not ready, because …', with any warnings"), never as a user story.

Parent gives one line: "Ready without a domain (fn-724): the ready check gives its answer without the domain." The child adds the exact inputs (`intents`, `domain`, `depends_on`, the `**Stage:**` line), the met-intent rule, the missing-intent-page rule, the holding-folder case, the unknown-capability case, the done-list behavior and exit codes. Detail clearly increases. The parent's "partly ready" answer maps onto the child's "workable true" plus warnings ("reports workable true with the warning ..."), consistent with the parent's ICE line "cap-723 is partly ready ... its only gap is no domain".

What: "A capability is ready when it serves a confirmed business intent and nothing it needs is open ... A missing domain is a warning, never a block." Why: "That rule blocked a plan built directly from a business intent. This functionality removes that block." Edges: "The check that a need or identified-by link points at a real capability or functionality ... (fn-725) owns that"; "Deciding which node to work on next ... Build a plan (cap-718) and /next do that". Jargon is defined in place ("the spine (the file that lists each node and its links)", "The ICE is the short agent intent of the node", the holding folder).
